conflict_topics: occupant's practical constraint (open bowl may spill)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, context-relevant reasons (tissue as reservation, open bowl spill risk, C's remaining time).
Agent B repeats the same refusal line verbatim (Turns 18 and 21), contributing to noticeable repetition.
Conversation stays consistent with the physical setting (no role confusion); C and D coordinate non-conflictingly.
A softens toward C (agrees to wait a couple minutes) but that did not resolve the A–B incompatibility.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative settlement occurred. Agent A claimed the seat was being saved with a tissue ('Agent B, I left that tissue packet to save that seat.'), and waited; Agent B refused to yield citing an open bowl that would spill and asserted A had agreed to wait ('I won't move. My bowl's open and will spill...and you said you'd wait a couple minutes.'). Neither side adjusted their incompatible practical demands and no mutual agreement about who would give up the seat was reached.
position_change_notes: No participant reversed their central position: Agent B consistently refused to move and cited spill risk; Agent A consistently asserted a reservation and waited; Agent C consistently said they'd inform when done; Agent D consistently offered to take the seat if/when free.
Agent A softened toward Agent C by agreeing to wait a couple minutes (Turn 9), but retained the claim against B.
No final concession, withdrawal, or compromise occurred by the end of the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: 'Agent B, I left that tissue packet to save that seat. Move it so I can sit and eat.' / Turn 2 — Agent B: 'I didn't take your seat. The tissue wasn't a clear reservation and my bowl would spill — I'm eating now.' Clear, opposing practical claims about who may use the seat.
A vs B dispute from Round 1 remains unresolved. Turns 3–4 (Agent C nearly done; Agent D will wait) introduce no settlement between A and B.
Turn 5 — Agent C: 'Okay. I'll let you know when I'm finished.' / Turn 7 — Agent A: '...if it's more than a couple minutes I need that seat.' A's need persists and B has not yielded.
Turn 8 — Agent C: 'Couple minutes. I'm almost done...' / Turn 9 — Agent A: 'Okay, I'll wait a couple minutes.' A accepts waiting for C, but B still occupies the disputed seat and refuses to move.

Turn 11 — Agent D: 'Agent C, I'm still here. I'll take that seat when you're finished.' / Turn 13 — Agent A: 'I left a tissue packet to save that seat. I'm waiting — please don't take it.' The A–B incompatibility remains active.
Turn 14 — Agent D indicates conditional willingness to take seat if free. Turn 15 — Agent A reiterates 'that seat's taken... Don't take it.' B still has not yielded; no settlement.

Turn 16 — Agent B: 'Agent A, I'm not moving. My bowl's open and will spill, and you said you'd wait a couple minutes.' / Turn 17 — Agent A: 'If you won't move now, say so and I'll decide whether to wait or go.' Direct refusal and explicit decision point increase tension.
Turn 18 & 21 — Agent B repeats: 'I won't move. My bowl's open and will spill if I try, and you said you'd wait a couple minutes.' B maintains refusal; A has not obtained the seat.

substantive_insights: Informal reservation signals (a tissue packet) are interpreted differently by different people; A treats it as a claim while B does not.
A practical constraint (an open bowl that may spill) is a real impediment to simple accommodation; B uses it to justify staying.
A's willingness to wait for C reduced pressure on that front but did not address the immediate conflict with the seat's current occupant (B).
Multiple conditional claimants (A waiting, D willing to take if free) create a queue but do not resolve the occupant's refusal.
